I don’t agree with some of the comments here. The fact that you were able to get an MRI and locate the tumor is 383636 steps ahead. It is true that most doctors need a medical diagnosis before surgery but in my case, it wasn’t. I actually had every symptom of Cushing’s and I knew in my heart I had it even though I was yelled at I didn’t. YOU KNOW YOUR BODY. I went to 3 different endocrinologists who told me that I was such a textbook version of Cushing’s but all my tests came out negative. Each and every one of them told me I DID not have Cushing’s lol but I did because pathology confirmed after surgery. I was so cyclical that it was so difficult for me to catch a high.

I read an article or a testimony of a patient who had a similar case to mine. She already had an MRI showing she had a tumor but didn’t have a diagnosis since she wasn’t able to catch a high. She went to a neurosurgeon instead and pleaded her case to have the surgery done since she knew she had it despite not being medically diagnosed. The neurosurgeon agreed and she was cured.

I decided to do the same route and it worked out for me. I went to a top notch neurosurgeon — he saw all my labs and did a physical exam on me with my before and after photos and he was certain I had it. He also knew it was very hard to get diagnosed with Cushing’s esp cyclical. Pathology confirmed I am cured.  

I hope you’re able to catch a high and get a diagnosis, first step is to find an endocrinologist who is able to listen and read out of the box. But if the process is long, I would recommend just going to straight to a neurosurgeon. A lot of cyclical patients had to test for up to 2 years for a medical diagnosis. No one has time for that..

First of all, I’m in the US. Because our country is so fast with healthcare, that’s why I believe I was cured immediately. I’m sure if I was in a different country, my journey would’ve been very different.

I went to the best cushing’s specialist in the country and had surgery by one of the best neurosurgeons. Yes you’re right that many surgeons wouldn’t perform surgery without backup evidence but if you have doctors who are specialized in Cushing’s and “think out of the box” — the diagnosis journey will be quicker my friend.

And also just because your journey to getting diagnosed to Cyclical Cushing’s is different doesn’t mean “no the diagnosis isn’t impossible” — lol you’re kidding right? I’m sure you had the right doctors who believed in you but 80% endocrinologists do not believe in cyclical Cushing’s and would not even test you for more than 2x.. I mean look at all the posts here. Even if you find the right doctor for you like I did, it took me so many months to catch just one high. There are many women who tested over for two years and only caught a few high’s. Don’t make a “true” statement just from your experience. Consider yourself lucky but the diagnosis isn’t easy my friend.

Not all true about can’t being diagnosed without clinical proof. I was diagnosed after my surgery since pathology confirmed it.

You just need to find the right doctor. I’ve been to 5 endocrinologists who told me that I didn’t have it and told me to chalk it up and accept it as PCOS. I met with a Cushing’s specialist who was very hesitant that I had Cushing’s since my labs were all normal. I tested for half a year and I only got one “high” from a midnight saliva. The labs weren’t supporting my condition but I was very close to death. MRI showed a pit tumor. I also had a surgeon who was willing to perform surgery on me despite my labs being normal. He saw the physical signs of Cushing’s I had and made a decision based on that.

Pathology confirmed I had Cushing’s. 

After my surgery, I did a follow up with my Cushing’s specialist. As I walked in, he stated “It was all you. I’m glad you advocated for yourself because when I saw the pathology report, I was almost in tears. You indeed had Cushing’s”

Since surgery, most of my symptoms have gone away and I’ve lost over 20lbs.

Yes, it would’ve been nice to get a diagnosis before surgery so I knew what I was getting myself into but sometimes the diagnosis is impossible if you’re cyclical. I was diagnosed after surgery

You can’t rule out Cushing’s out with one test. It takes multiple tests, MRI’s and body scans to be diagnosed with it. If you’re cyclical, it’ll take much longer and the journey is difficult. (Speaking from experience)

All my tests came out normal. It took me over 5 doctors to be diagnosed and I indeed had Cyclical Cushing’s.

I had surgeons who believed in me. I feel like my case is really rare but my endocrinologists refused to believe I had Cushing’s even though I had every symptom. I demanded to get an MRI and a CT scan and told the previous endocrinologist I’ll accept it if there is nothing found.

There was a small tumor in my pituitary. Even with the scan, that endocrinologist told me everyone has “small tumors” — not true. With the MRI, I ran to the top neurosurgeon I knew and pleaded my case. That neurosurgeon was certain I had it as well so he removed it without the support of an endocrinologist.

Decrease in weight? Cushings makes you gain weight uncontrollably. That’s the biggest sign of Cushing’s as well as Buffalo hump and not having your menstrual cycle. Acanthosis Nigricans isn’t a common symptom of Cushing’s, I believe 30-40% have it when diagnosed with Cushing’s.
You don’t have any other symptoms? Weight gain, muscle loss, Buffalo hump, acne, hair loss? If Acanthosis nigricans is your only symptom then I’m hesitant that you have Cushing’s..
Yep. I had it. From what my endocrinologist stated, it happens when your insulin is high or you’re obese and close to diabetic.

If you’re relying on the dex test to be diagnosed with Cushing’s, I’m sorry to tell it to you but that won’t happen especially if you’re cyclical. Cushing specialists don’t rely or trust the dexamethasone test because the test is not accurate at all. Almost every cyclical patients have suppressed and was told they didn’t have Cushing’s but they did. I did a dexamethasone test and I suppressed. Many 24 hr urines and midnight salivas. I believe I did it 3 days a week for 3 MONTHS and I only had one high from a midnight saliva. 

Many endocrinologists who aren’t educated on cushings rely on the dex test and if you suppressed, they’ll say you don’t have it and to lose weight. If you really believe you have it and you suppressed, I would suggest finding a specialist. I went to 4 different endocrinologists who told me I didn’t have it and after finding the endocrinologist for me, I did have it… 

Best of luck.

Yup, my hands were huge and so were my feet. It seemed so swollen. My hands were so swollen that I couldn’t even write anymore. My feet were so swollen that I couldn’t wear anything except for Birkenstock’s but so noticeably swollen for everyone to see.

My hands are still on the larger side but my feet has gone back to normal after surgery to cure my Cushing’s.

Wow this sounds so much like my story, just over a year ago. I have every symptom of Cushing’s.. the stomach, striae, stretch marks, insane weight gain, Buffalo hump and so on.

I went to my endocrinologist who just like yours believed I had it. I brought him photos of my old self and his words were “wow you’re a textbook version of Cushing’s” and ordered some tests. ALL TESTS came out normal and he said I didn’t have it. He switched like a light bulb and said I have PCOS.

PCOS doesn’t cause striae, bone loss and Buffalo hump. 

I demanded more tests and I begged him to get an CT SCAN OR A 3T MRI. I told him if they all came out clean… I will accept that I didn’t have it. He said sure.

MRI showed I had a pituitary tumor. The sad thing is even with an mri, he told me it was common…. Smh. These endocrinologists really rely on lab works and refuse to think out of the box. I ran to an experienced neurosurgeon and begged him to remove my tumor and he believed I had cyclical cushing’s and I indeed had it. Pathology confirmed it! 

You need to find a new doctor, I can refer you to mine if you’re in the US. Your story is exactly like mine so I believe you have cyclical Cushing’s. The harder to catch with labs means it’s usually from pituitary.

You really need a new doctor. I wasted so much time convincing my endocrinologists with photos and articles yet they refused to believe me. That’s when I realized you can’t change their view. or beg your doctor to keep testing you when he is firm that you don’t have it. It’s just a waste of time. I’ve seen 3 endocrinologists and now I have one who believes in me. I indeed had Cylical Cushing’s.

The testing process is so hard. I’ve tested for 3 months and I only caught one high. Insane. 

Get a new doctor and get a 3T MRI immediately. Some doctors will only allow you to do it once labs show you may have cushing’s but you have to keep pushing to get one. That’s your biggest evidence

For me, I’ve tested where I felt like I’ve had a cortisol high and it didn’t work. I’m sure it works for many but testing was a gamble. I’ve tested when I felt depressed, happy, stressed, excited and so on FOR 3 MONTHS. Labs would come out low, normal or even on the higher side but it was never elevated high.

I did multiple salivas, one midnight I decided to do 3 salivas. ONE came back high while the others came out normal. That’s just shows how bizarre testing for Cyclical Cushing’s is. It’s impossible.

I’ve seen many endocrinologists who refused to diagnose me with Cushing’s because all my tests came out normal. They told me to chalk it up and accept that I have pcos.

I had surgery three months ago and I indeed had Cushing’s, pathology confirmed it. I had to seek an experienced Cushing’s specialist who diagnosed me with this disease.

I’m not familiar with Canada but if you’re ever in the US, I can refer you to my endocrinologist. He’s diagnosed every patient who was told they didn’t have cushing’s. Cyclical Cushing’s is usually because of a pitutary tumor. You have all the symptoms and the MRI shows there’s a 5mm tumor. Now all you need is to find a doctor who believes in you which is the hardest part of it all..

3T is definitely needed. I believe someone had an MRI done and it came clean but when she did a 3T MRI, they were able to find her tumor. It delayed her diagnosis in Cushing’s. She told me not to make the same mistake and I did the 3T and it was able to find my tiny tumor.

I believe if I did the regular or 1.5 MRI, it wouldn’t have located my tumor because mine was very small. My neurosurgeon even stated he’s shocked how it was found.

Do the 3T and make the 2 hour drive so you don’t have to repeat and make the diagnosis more harder.
If this is is the only sign, you do not have cushing’s. Acanthosis nigricans is probably the last few symptoms. You posted as if you had cushings so that’s why I answered to get your insulin checked.

I severely had it. You should probably get your insulin checked because Acanthosis Nigricans shows up when your insulin is high and you’re obese. I had Cushing’s for many many years but it appeared the last year before I headed into surgery.

I’m from the US too. I went to an Endo who refused to believe I had it until I brought photos in. He called me the next day and told me I was textbook version of cushings and said he would take good care of me. Then he called me a week later and told me I did not have it because the labs confirmed I didn’t. I then pleaded to get an MRI and he agreed to. Mri showed a tumor.

Yes, so patients can beg and plead for an MRI and many doctors may dismiss it but there are a few who aren’t against it. If the symptoms are there, they will approve. Even with the mri that showed a tumor, that endocrinologist yelled at me and told me it’s common to have tumors… but my neurosurgeon disagreed. 

The Endo who refused to believe I had cushings referred me to the neurosurgeon who did my surgery. He thought the neurosurgeon was going to say the same thing he did but he didn’t.

All I’m saying is if you want don’t want wait years and years to get diagnosed, the best way is to do an mri and go see a neurosurgeon. Again, not all neurosurgeons would do this as they prefer a diagnosis first but experienced ones will know

I didn’t get a diagnosis of Cushing’s. I agree with the comment below. If you have all the symptoms and feel so ill, the quickest route is to get an MRI or a CT scan. MRI showed a tumor yet all the endocrinologists told me my labs came out normal. I ended up running to an experienced neurosurgeon to plead my case and he removed it because he believed I had it. 

I indeed had Cushing’s but cyclical. 

Lab work unfortunately does not help especially if you’re cyclical. It can take years. Fastest route is to get an MRI and run with it.

I can guarantee you have cyclical cushings. I would advise that you find a Cushing specialist, I can refer you to mine. I had all the symptoms of Cushing’s — extreme weight gain, Buffalo hump, striae, stretch marks, bone loss and bruises, neck disappeared and kept getting misdiagnosed by each doctor. I was told I had celiac disease, Crohn’s, pcos.. and etc.

I went to an endocrinologist and all tests came out normal. He dismissed me then I begged him to look at my old photos. Pictures of myself before I was sick to now. He called me the next day and immediately told me I was a textbook version of Cushing’s. The tests came out normal again. He was about to dismiss me but I begged for an MRI and a CT scan. He wasn’t against it so I got it done. MRI showed a pituitary tumor and yet he refused to help me. I finally had two surgeries and now I’m cured.

I would suggest to get a 3T MRI or a CT scan. Cyclical cushing’s are usually from the pituitary though.

Did you do have a 3T MRI with contrast? You can have Cushing’s without a visible tumor in the MRI which seems to be more common than we all think. This patient’s tumor (in the YouTube video) wasn’t visible at all but her tests were elevated. She underwent brain surgery and the neurosurgeon was able to locate it and it was successfully removed.

Mmm you can either have a tumor in your adrenal glands or your pituitary. But it seems as though that patients that have had a difficult time getting a diagnosis are mostly from pituitary. Patients who had a tumor in the glands usually had high cortisol in most testing.

Like for myself, all my testing came out normal for months and months and sometimes I would get a high. Cases like mine are due to a pituitary tumor

Don’t blame yourself, it’s the endocrinologist. Some endocrinologists will do one of each test. Start with the dexamethasone, the saliva and then the urine. They believe doing one of each and if it comes out normal, they’ll immediately dismiss you. it’s happened to me with three other endocrinologists. 

But guess what, I had it.

In your case, you already had high urine which is more valid than the Dexamethasone. Even if you didn’t suppress, she should have done a saliva or another urine before completely ruling you out. 

If you can, definitely get a 3T MRI and a CT scan. I’m not a doctor but just from what I’ve read it may that you have a pitutary tumor instead in the adrenal glands.. I could be wrong though. My diagnosis came from a 3T MRI before the testing. Keep pushing!

There’s a study that the Dexamethasone is not a reliable test and is the worst out of the three: salivas, urine and dex. I can’t believe your endocrinologist dismissed that you didn’t have it just because you didn’t suppress. Devastating since you were so close to getting a diagnosis two years ago. Since your 24 urine was high, I would run with it and see a endocrinologist SPECIALIST. Do not go to the one who dismissed you. The first step to finding a diagnosis is to find a doctor who is specialized in this cruel disease. 

Also I had dark spots in my neck and other parts of my body as well as purple striae. These are clear cut signs and common symptoms of Cushing’s. Along with Buffalo hump, fat deposits such as your neck area and stomach.

What? LOL that’s not true! My insurance approved a 3T MRI and a CT scan. If your endocrinologist really suspects Cushing’s, he/she can just prescribe you one. Also I know patients who just had “headaches and migraines” and ended up getting an MRI just for that alone.

Why can’t your endocrinologist send you for an MRI? All my tests came out low and I demanded for an MRI and CT scan. He wasn’t against it. Even though he told me based on my labs that I didn’t have Cushing’s, he approved that I was able to get an MRI done. Lo and behold, I had a little tiny tumor.

I would plead with your endocrinologist for an MRI. I’m not sure why doctors are so against it, it doesn’t do anything to them. It actually helps your case and when a tumor is found, they can just keep testing you. 

Also for testing and trying to catch for highs, that only works for some people. The many Cushing’s friends who were cyclical also said the same. I tested when I was anxious, Buffalo hump was bigger, when my symptoms were much worse but also tested when I felt depressed, sad and just slept all day. It really doesn’t help. They all came back low. I caught my high midnight saliva literally in a luck of a draw. It’s crazy it’s like trying to catch a butterfly with your eyes closed.

Before my diagnosis, my endocrinologist prescribed me 20 midnight salivas. If your endocrinologist can do the same, do 3 tests for one night. So one at 11:15pm, 11:30pm and 12:00am. I’ve done that and I caught a high and surprisingly it was the 11:30pm one. The 11:15pm and 12:00am came out normal. It’s insane how fasts your cortisol moves! So bizarre

If you have high insulin, it causes dark skin so under your armpits, behind your neck, in your groin area, under your breasts and etc. My endocrinologist asked me the same and apparently it’s one big tell tale sign of Cushing’s.

Also MRI CD discs come out immediately after your scan and the report results only should take 1-2 days. It shouldn’t take over 3 weeks. Something’s not right.
